In this Year 4 English lesson, pupils explore adverbs and adverbial phrases in depth, learning how they add information about how, when, where, how often and in what order actions happen.

This lesson includes:
✔ Recognising the difference between a single adverb and an adverbial phrase
✔ Sorting adverbials according to how, when and where
✔ Understanding adverbials of frequency and possibility
✔ Using frequency words such as regularly, frequently, usually, rarely and occasionally
✔ Using possibility words such as perhaps, maybe, certainly, possibly and probably
✔ Identifying adverbials in short passages and classifying them by function
✔ Revisiting adverbials of time, place, number, frequency and manner
✔ Completing sentences with suitable adverbials of time and place
✔ Using sequencing adverbials such as firstly, secondly, next and finally
✔ Using adverbials of manner to explain how an action happens
✔ Sorting single words, phrases and prepositional phrases into adverbial categories
✔ Writing sentences containing adverbials of time, place, frequency and manner
✔ Organising instructions with adverbials of number
✔ Understanding that adverbs can modify other adverbs
✔ Identifying verbs and adverbs in sentences
✔ Understanding how adverbs can modify adjectives

Pupils begin by exploring adverbial phrases and how they give extra information about an action. They compare single adverbs with longer adverbial phrases and sort examples by whether they tell us how, when or where something happens.

The lesson then focuses on frequency and possibility. Pupils learn how words such as always, sometimes, rarely, usually, perhaps and certainly express how often something happens or how likely an event is, and they apply this understanding in sorting and reading activities.

Later sections revisit a wider range of adverbials: time, place, number, frequency and manner. Pupils complete sentences, sort examples and write their own sentences using different types of adverbial accurately.

The lesson also develops sequencing language for instructions, including firstly, secondly, next, then and finally, and shows how adverbs can modify other adverbs and adjectives to make meaning more precise.

By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to identify and classify a wide range of adverbs and adverbial phrases, use them to add precise detail to sentences, and explain how adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs.
